key_insight: An AE-GCN-LSTM surrogate can forecast multicomponent, multiphase microstructure evolution in high-entropy alloys far beyond the training horizon while preserving key morphology and composition trends.
engineering_relevance: This enables orders-of-magnitude faster phase-field-style simulation for alloy design, large-domain scaling, and high-throughput screening.
method: Multi-head autoencoder compresses four concentration fields plus phase-field order parameter into latent variables.
Latent states are converted into graphs and propagated with GCN-LSTM for spatial-temporal forecasting.
Model is trained on 100×100 AlCrFeNi phase-field simulations and then transferred to larger and unseen conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate forecasting up to 3,000,000 timesteps and speedups of about 7,200 to 62,300× across unseen precipitate configurations, larger domains, and new compositions.
watch_item: The surrogate is validated from a single nominal training composition and phase-field dataset, so generalization outside the evaluated alloy/physics space may still require careful verification.
paper_title: Deep Learning for Accelerated Long-Horizon Forecasting of Multicomponent Multiphase Microstructure Evolution in High-Entropy Alloys
